Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Sister-cell/clonal recurrence test of AP-1 memory heritability ("recur")
ideas.description: Barcode a population (e.g., Watermelon/ClonMapper-style lineage barcodes), stimulate transiently, then let clones expand and re-stimulate: if AP-1 is a memory mechanism, the magnitude of the secondary AP-1 response should be far more correlated among cells sharing a barcode than among unrelated cells, and that intraclonal correlation should decay with a measurable number of divisions. Combine with split-clone designs (one half naive, one half primed) and single-cell multiome to show the heritable unit is AP-1 motif accessibility rather than a generic proliferative state.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking by FOS/JUN at memory enhancers ("dyaster")
ideas.description: Test whether AP-1 remains chromatin-bound through mitosis by performing CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag for FOS/JUN and ATAC-seq on mitotically arrested and sorted primed vs. naive cells, paired with live-cell Halo-JUN imaging and FRAP on condensed chromosomes to measure residence time. Then test necessity with a cell-cycle-restricted auxin/dTAG degron that removes AP-1 only during the M-phase window, asking whether daughter cells lose the primed response while cells degraded in G1 retain it.

ideas.title: Degron epistasis separating writing, maintenance, and reading ("unmask")
ideas.description: Using dTAG- or auxin-tagged endogenous FOS/JUN (and a FOS-family-wide degron to handle redundancy), degrade AP-1 in three nonoverlapping windows — during the priming stimulus, during the quiescent memory interval, and only at re-stimulation — and score secondary response amplitude, latency, and enhancer accessibility. This distinguishes AP-1 as the writer that unmasks latent enhancers, as a continuously required maintenance factor, or merely as the reader that exploits a trace stored by other means (e.g., H3K4me1, CTCF loops, DNA methylation).

ideas.title: Dose- and pulse-layering to test accretive memory ("serpulidan")
ideas.description: Deliver controlled trains of stimulus pulses (varying number, amplitude, and spacing, ideally with optogenetic or small-molecule-gated AP-1 input) and ask whether primed AP-1 enhancer accessibility and secondary output accumulate in discrete, stimulus-countable increments rather than tracking only the most recent or the integrated dose. Fitting the resulting response surface discriminates a genuine accretive recorder from a slow-relaxation filter, and identifies the subset of "layer-forming" AP-1 sites for follow-up.

ideas.title: Single-molecule footprinting of the residual trace ("limacel")
ideas.description: Apply single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (SMF/Fiber-seq) at AP-1 memory enhancers days after the stimulus has decayed, to distinguish on individual DNA fibers between persistent low-level AP-1 occupancy, a bound-factor-free but nucleosome-depleted "empty shell," and fully reclosed chromatin. Quantifying the fraction of molecules in each state, and how that fraction predicts single-cell secondary response by paired scSMF/transcriptome readout, tests whether the stored trace is a structural remnant rather than ongoing signaling.
